title: EngineState (C3 base state, STORED form)
description: The PERSISTED form of engine_state.yaml -- machine-owned, always carries its own state_rev. docs/COACHING_LOOP_SPEC.md, C3: 'Base engine state (engine_state.yaml, machine-owned): season = {active_goal_id, phase_calendar (block/week table with date bounds), resolution_input_hash}; cursor = {block_number, week_in_block}; bike series levels; ownership registry; recent_races (rolling 28-day window). NOTHING about proposals/approvals lives here.' This is NOT the same schema as engine_state_next in a ProposalIR: `engine_state_next` is the base-state-view HASH INPUT ('the stored state_rev field is set to this value and is NOT part of the view'), so it must never carry state_rev -- see coaching_loop/schemas/engine_state_base_view.schema.json, which this file's non-state_rev properties are kept in sync with by hand.

state_rev.description: H(base-state-view) of this same object with state_rev removed -- i.e. H() of this object validated against engine_state_base_view.schema.json. Excluded from hashing by coaching_loop.hashing.base_state_view.

resolution_input_hash.description: Hash of the persisted inputs the season resolver ran on (goal + dossier fields). SHA-256 hex, per 'Hash algorithm everywhere: SHA-256.' A mismatch on the next run triggers season re-resolution and cursor re-anchoring (C3, GOAL/DOSSIER CHANGE).

ownership_registry.description: TP workout ids the loop owns, keyed by week_start (ISO date). Used by the v1.1+ op-grammar preflight (replace/delete targets must be loop-owned) and by A1/A2 windowing (loop-owned sessions only). Keys are constrained to date strings so this map cannot be used to smuggle in proposal/journal-shaped data under an arbitrary key name.

recent_races.description: Rolling 28-day window, refreshed on APPROVE from the approved week's races. The W-1 lookback source.
